CTIS 151.name: Introduction to Programming
CTIS 151.description: An introduction to programming from both design and programming standpoints. Syntax and semantics of programming languages, programming style, program debugging and testing, data representation, simple arithmetic expressions, decision and control statements, using arrays, introduction to standard libraries, structured and modular programming techniques will be covered using C language.

CTIS 152.name: Algorithms and Data Structures
CTIS 152.description: Implementation of abstract data types and structures. Dynamic data structures. Strings, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees and graphs. Multidimensional structures. Recursion. Implementation of basic searching and sorting methods. Binary File I/O.

CTIS 163.name: Discrete Mathematics
CTIS 163.description: An introductory course in discrete mathematics. The course covers logic and elements of logic, quantifiers, proofs, mathematical induction, functions and relations. Graph theory, theory of trees, Boolean algebras and combinational circuits, finite-state machines.

CTIS 164.name: Technical Mathematics with Programming
CTIS 164.description: The fundamental concepts in technical mathematics and precalculus using programming. Functions and graphs, linear equations, plane analytic geometry, quadratic equations, trigonometry, vectors, matrices and determinants.

CTIS 165.name: Fundamentals of Information Systems
CTIS 165.description: The fundamental concepts of information systems with historical and evolutionary perspectives. Systems, organizational and strategic role and added value of information systems, decision support systems, data mining, Management information systems (MIS), information systems planning, data management, computer networking, internet, analysis, design, development, and maintenance of information systems, competitive edge of information systems.

CTIS 166.name: Information Technologies
CTIS 166.description: The basic operating system concepts by using Linux operating system. Linux GUI, kernel, CUI, shells, basic shell programming, Linux file system architecture, file security, Linux tools for software developments.

CTIS 186.name: Business Computer Applications
CTIS 186.description: Presentation software, word processing, spreadsheet applications. Presentation software: file operations, speaker operations, slide shows, presentation planning and design, reviews, objects, transitions and animations, page setups, navigation, templates, views, slide reuse, sections, themes, smartart, wordart, audio and video operations. Word processor: editing, customizing, viewing, readability features, document properties, font attributes, formatting, styles, objects, and tables. Spreadsheet software: environment, cells/columns/rows, formulas, editing, formatting, styles, data types, worksheets, tabs, referencing, functions, lookup tables, data sources, charts, large data sets, data tables, sorting, filtering, rules, and conditional formatting.

CTIS 221.name: Object Oriented Programming
CTIS 221.description: Object oriented programming paradigm by focusing on the principal concepts such as objects, classes, encapsulation, modular design and hierarchy between classes, inheritance, polymorphism and abstract classes using Java language. In addition to the principal concepts, some advanced subjects of object oriented programming will be covered such as multi-Frame, Java I/O, file operators, object serialization, Generics, Collections.

CTIS 222.name: Object Oriented Analysis and Design
CTIS 222.description: The object-oriented (OO) modelling, which manages the complexity inherent in many different kinds of systems, has proven to be a very powerful and unifying concept. The course describes fundamental principles of OO modeling, foundations of evolutionary requirements analysis, and the principles and guidelines on OO analysis and design. Topics include the specification of software requirements, OO analysis approaches, dynamic and static modeling with the Unified Modeling Language (UML v2.X), OO design, and software implementation concerns. Moreover, the course not only describes the assessment of the qualities of object design alternatives but also introduces the mapping of design artifacts to the source code. This hands-on course is designed for students with Java background.

CTIS 255.name: Frontend Web Technologies
CTIS 255.description: The fundamentals of interactive web interface development; core web frontend technologies. HTML structure; CSS styling; responsive design principles; JavaScript programming; DOM interaction; event-based behavior.

CTIS 256.name: Introduction to Backend Development
CTIS 256.description: The design and implementation of backend systems for web and mobile applications. HTTP request/response handling; form processing; package management; input validation; session and cookie management; web security (hashing, XSS, CSRF, SQL injection); multi-user systems; CRUD operations; file uploading; API-driven, asynchronous single-page applications.

CTIS 259.name: Database Management Systems and Applications
CTIS 259.description: Fundamentals of SQL, Views, Constraints, Triggers, Transaction Processing, User Privileges, programming with PL/SQL, Oracle forms and reports with practice in Oracle Database Management System. Relational Algebra. Logical database design: Relational Data Model, Entity-Relationship (E-R) Diagrams, Functional Dependency and Normalization.

CTIS 261.name: Fundamentals of Computer Networks
CTIS 261.description: Introduction to computer networks. LANs, WANs and Internetworks. Protocols and Layered models. The Open System Interconnection (OSI) model. TCP/IP model. Application Layer Protocols and services: DNS, www, e-mail, FTP, DHCP, P2P, Telnet. OSI Transport Layer: TCP and UDP protocols. OSI Network Layer: IPv4 protocol and addressing: Special addresses, subnetting. Routing. Data-Link Layer: Media access control techniques. MAC addressing and framing. Ethernet protocol concepts and types. OSI Physical Layer: Signalling and encoding. Physical media. Planning and cabling networks. Basic network configuration and testing. Network Security Fundamentals.

CTIS 262.name: Applied Computer Networks
CTIS 262.description: This course covers Switching, Routing and Wireless Essentials related topics. The covered topics include the architecture, components, and operations of routers and switches in a small network. Students learn how to configure and secure a router, wireless home router and a switch for basic functionality. Additionally, various network security concepts are studied together with real life scenarios and device configurations.

CTIS 264.name: Computer Algorithms
CTIS 264.description: Time and space analysis of algorithms; problem solving techniques. Sorting; searching; divide and conquer algorithms; dynamic programming; greedy algorithms; graph algorithms; string matching algorithms.

CTIS 266.name: Applied Linear Algebra for Artificial Intelligence
CTIS 266.description: Vectors and matrices. Vector operations, geometric interpretation of vectors, dot and cross products, projections, and applications in three-dimensional geometry. Matrix multiplication and linear transformations. Linear equations, existence and classification of solutions, Gaussian elimination and LU decomposition. Inverse matrices and determinants. Vector spaces, span, basis, dimension, and rank. Orthogonality, the Gram - Schmidt process, QR decomposition, and least-squares approximation. Characteristic equation of a matrix: eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

CTIS 285.name: Hospitality Industry Computerization
CTIS 285.description: Introduction to introduce students to the principles of MIS (Management Information Systems). Exploration of the role of Information in operational and management decision making in the hotel industry. Using a simulated hotel and a live property management system. Experiencing the day-to-day activities performed at each stage of the "guest-cycle", from reservations, room assignment and check-in to check-out, payment and departure. Designed to meet both the front-office and back-office requirements of any size hotel or hotel chain. Hands-on experience in the many facets of hotel management.

CTIS 286.name: Food and Beverage Computer Applications
CTIS 286.description: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the computerization of in the hospitality industry. Through a widely-used computer application package, students will gain the ability to create the necessary database system for food and beverage management. They will learn the relationship between the food and beverage department and suppliers; how to make issues between the hotel stores, restaurants and suppliers, how to create sales items order procedures and purchasing, cost management of the sales outlets.

CTIS 290.name: Summer Internship
CTIS 290.description: First exposure to the workplace, in a supervised setting. Assignments scheduled and monitored through CTIS Internship Coordinator. Observation of an organization via provided IS/IT solutions and obtaining practical real-life experience. A minimum of twenty (20) working days, undertaken during the summer months following the completion of the second academic year. An internship report to be submitted upon completion of the program.

CTIS 310.name: Semester Internship
CTIS 310.description: One semester work in industry the student with an opportunity to apply present knowledge in a real-life environment and to observe, document and evaluate the operations of a computing department. Presentation of an analysis of experience, identifying the factors contributing to the success and/or problems of the department.

CTIS 359.name: Principles of Software Engineering
CTIS 359.description: Software processes; requirements analysis and specification, design, development and testing methodologies, and software lifecycle. Importance of planning and managing the software processes. Software modeling, review of Unified Modeling Language and CASE technology. Software development, planning, management and engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 12207 and EIA/IEEE J-STD-016-1995. An in-depth introduction to the concepts and techniques for software development. Experience team-oriented software engineering through conventional software life cycle models via small-scale software project.

CTIS 363.name: Ethical and Social Issues in Information Systems
CTIS 363.description: Basic understanding of IT history, awareness of current issues, and familiarity with ethics. An overview of ethical theories and related problems with privacy, networking, security and reliability. Issues related to social networking, government surveillance, privacy, security, and intellectual property to allow students to become responsible and ethical professionals.

CTIS 365.name: Applied Data Analysis
CTIS 365.description: This course will provide an introduction to the important concepts in statistics with programming examples to make the connection between concepts and implementation. The focus throughout the course will be on developing an understanding of the rationale, the correct interpretation, and the appropriate applications of some of the most commonly used statistical techniques. The course will also familiarize students with essential software tools and techniques to acquire, prepare and visualize data for further statistical modeling and analysis. No previous research or statistical knowledge is assumed of the student. The emphasis will be on concepts and applications rather than on computations.

CTIS 386.name: Travel Technologies
CTIS 386.description: Providing the students knowledge and computerized practice for "Global Distribution Systems", via using an online travel reservation system as a tool, which lets agents or end users search, book and manage travel related activities.

CTIS 411.name: Senior Project I
CTIS 411.description: A capstone course and the first part of a yearlong senior team project. Teamwork on assigned projects to complete the initial phases of the software development lifecycle which are initial project plan, requirements specification, and software design. Development of a product prototype and its presentation before continuing to second part of this course which is "CTIS456 Senior Project II".

CTIS 417.name: Software Design Patterns
CTIS 417.description: Software quality attributes can be classified as internal and external. Code reusability, maintainability, and portability are the examples of internal software quality attributes. System performance, scalability, and availability are the examples of external software quality attributes. Design patterns in general describe the best practices for a specific type of design problem based on the fundamental design principles. Low-level software design patterns deal with the internal software quality attributes. High-level architectural design patterns deal with the external software quality attributes. This course teaches students how to design quality software systems by applying both the software and architectural design patterns. In this course, application of design patterns is based on object-oriented methodology by using JAVA.

CTIS 456.name: Senior Project II
CTIS 456.description: A capstone course and the second part of a yearlong senior team project. Later phases of the software development lifecycle which are project implementation and testing.

CTIS 465.name: Microservice Development
CTIS 465.description: Microservice Architecture using RESTful Web Services behind a Gateway developed with ASP.NET Core Web API and C# Programming Language. More on Object Oriented Programming and database CRUD operations using Entity Framework Core ORM. Clean Architecture including Dependency Injection, CQRS and Mediator Design Patterns, SOLID Principles, Docker.

CTIS 466.name: Business Process Management
CTIS 466.description: Business process definition; business process analysis; business process identification; business process automation; business process monitoring and control; business process design; business process implementation; business transformation; business process reengineering; organizational restructuring; business and information technology alignment; business process modelling; Business Process Modelling Notation.

CTIS 470.name: Cross-platform Application Development
CTIS 470.description: Cross-platform frameworks and their comparison. Introduction to an open-source UI software development kit. Installation, project creation, project folder structure, execution of the application on different platforms. Fundamentals of a programming language used to develop web and mobile applications. Creation of UI with fundamental widgets. State management. Event handling and gesture detection. Navigation and routing. Validation. Animation. Networking. Data persistency. Related cloud computing services.

CTIS 471.name: Introduction to Applied Machine Learning
CTIS 471.description: Definition, motivation and applications of machine learning. Supervised methods: linear regression, decision trees, support vector machines, and artificial neural networks. Unsupervised methods with clustering algorithms. Learning theory. Performance metrics of machine learning methods.

CTIS 472.name: Human Computer Interaction
CTIS 472.description: General discipline of Human Computer Interaction (HCI). Issues of human factors and the design of computer application interfaces. Psychological and social aspects of HCI. Real-world examples of VR, AR, web and mobile applications. Individual and/or team work to design, implement, and evaluate various interactive systems and user interfaces. Theoretical knowledge and practical experience in the fundamental aspects of human perception, cognition, and learning. Design, implementation, and evaluation of interfaces.

CTIS 473.name: Cloud Computing Foundations
CTIS 473.description: Cloud concepts overview. Cloud economics and billing. Overview of cloud security, architecture, pricing and support. Cloud storage. Cloud databases. Compute services. Practice and lab work with widely accepted cloud service providers.

CTIS 474.name: Information Systems Auditing
CTIS 474.description: This course examines the key principles and applied techniques related to Information Systems Auditing processes and related controls and is designed to meet the increasing needs of audit, compliance, security and risk management professionals. This course also give the skills necessary to perform an audit on information systems, including obtaining evidence on the reliability of the systems, safeguarding of information assets/processes, and constructing risk profiles of information systems applications in according to standards and frameworks.

CTIS 475.name: Architecting Scalable Software
CTIS 475.description: Developing an understanding of architectural patterns and principles of software design. Identifying the quality attributes of a system, evaluating architectural patterns and using them to make architectural decisions. Comprehending "scalability" and everything it entails, with the help of case studies. Designing and developing scalable solutions as microservices. Containerizing microservices and deploying them on a serverless architecture.

CTIS 476.name: Software Architectures for Simulation and Modelling
CTIS 476.description: Simulation is an interdisciplinary domain. This course focuses on software aspect of the simulation and modeling domain. Simulation concepts, types of simulations. Distributed simulations, levels of interoperability. HLA; motivations, history, standardization and services. Advanced HLA Concepts, federation development process. Conceptual Modeling; the role of common understanding, problems and solutions. Federation and federate design. Federate development and integration. Development activities will be in C++.

CTIS 477.name: Systems Engineering
CTIS 477.description: Systems engineering concepts, tools and standards. Systems engineering process including some applications. Requirements engineering discipline with systems approach including definitions, types, phases and tools. Requirements engineering applications with systems modeling and UML/SysML examples. System architectures including patterns and frameworks, system and subsystem design. System verification and validation together with test, integration, acceptance and maintenance phases. Modeling and simulation in system approach. Systems engineering management issues including planning, risk management, quality and configuration management. Some applications and examples for the actual technologies including AI, big data, IoT, smart cities, etc.

CTIS 478.name: Advanced Web Technologies
CTIS 478.description: This course provides advanced topics in web application development. It focuses on hot topics on client and server side languages, frameworks (javascript frameworks, server-side frameworks) , databases (relational and noSQL), design patterns (mvc, subscription) and software architectures (SOA, micro services). By this course, the students will be able to design and implement efficient, scalable, reusable, flexible front-end and back-end softwares for web and mobile applications.

CTIS 479.name: C# Programming in the .NET Framework
CTIS 479.description: This course introduces students to the .NET framework and provides the necessary skills and knowledge to design and develop applications in the .NET framework by using C# programming language. In this course, students will have hands-on experience on object oriented programming concepts with .NET framework features such as creating windows and web applications (ASP.NET), managing data with ADO.NET and Language-Integrated Query (LINQ), using Model View Controller (MVC) design pattern will be covered. Students who want to take this course must have good knowledge of object-oriented programming principles and have hands-on experience with an object-oriented programming language (e.g., C++, java).

CTIS 480.name: iOS Application Development
CTIS 480.description: A programming course for iOS enabled devices. Overview of iOS, App store, creating developer account, using Xcode, understanding iOS frameworks, understanding model-view-controller, learning Objective-C, learning Swift, using Storyboard, using Playground, using different view controllers, view controller lifecycle, understanding views outlets and actions, writing basic applications and testing them, alerts, timers, gestures, graphics and multimedia programming, persistence, documents and core data, file handling, database storage, accessing built-in applications, push notifications, web services, displaying maps, sensor programming, iCloud programming, Bonjour programming, Bluetooth programming.

CTIS 483.name: Database Administration
CTIS 483.description: Installing Oracle Software, Oracle Grid Infrastructure installation for a standalone server, Creating Database Using DBCA, Oracle Database Server Architecture, Managing Database Instance, Database Configurations, Memory Structures, Process Structures, Managing ASM Instance, Network Environment, Database Storage Architecture, Transactions, Administering User Security, Concurrency Control Mechanisms, Crash Recovery Components, Managing Undo-Redo Data, Database Auditing and Database Maintenance, Performance Management, Backup and Recovery Concepts, Moving Data, Database Restart. Whole content will be explained in Oracle environment and students will have rights to take Oracle Database 11g: Administration I 1Z0-052 exam as part of the Oracle Academy membership, and be able to take Oracle Database 11g Administrator Certified Associate (OCA).

CTIS 484.name: Advanced Topics in Programming
CTIS 484.description: Object oriented programming concepts using C++ programming language. Developing applications for processors with parallel computing resources. Fundamental concepts and in-depth knowledge about parallel, distributed, grid and cloud computing programming principles, programming GPUs (CUDA), communication models, memory utilization and limitations of these processors.

CTIS 485.name: Information Storage and Management
CTIS 485.description: Introduction to information storage systems, data protection using RAID, intelligent storage systems, storage networking and virtualization technologies, business continuity, local and remote replication techniques, cloud computing, storage security, monitoring and reporting.

CTIS 486.name: Linux System Administration
CTIS 486.description: Practical issues in Linux system administration. Installation, software management, and user management issues. Linux shell utilities, file system management, core system daemon, kernel and compilation concepts. Networking: TCP/IP and network configuration, local and network security with applications of Internet protocols like HTTP, SMTP, and DNS.

CTIS 487.name: Mobile Application Development
CTIS 487.description: Technical and business related challenges posed by current mobile devices and wireless communications. Comparison and selection of software tools and APIs to develop mobile applications while considering their popularity, scope and limitations. Development and testing of realistic applications for mobile devices.

CTIS 488.name: Data Analysis
CTIS 488.description: CTIS 488 is the second course offered in the department dealing with statistical methodology. The focus throughout the course will be on developing an understanding of the rationale, the correct interpretation, and the appropriate applications of some of the most commonly used statistical techniques. The broad object of this course is to acquaint students with the basic theory, methods, and most importantly, applications of commonly used statistical techniques such as ANOVA, correlation and regression, and Chi-square statistics. The emphasis will be on concepts and applications rather than on computations.

CTIS 489.name: Interactive Computer Graphics Programming
CTIS 489.description: 2D and 3D programming concepts to create interactive graphics applications such as simulators, computer games, real-time visualization applications using OpenGL API. Video hardware architecture, 2D/3D mathematics, GLUT library, 2D primitive drawing, 2D transformations, 2D animation, 3D object modeling and drawing, 3D transformations, perspective projection, orthogonal projection, hidden surface removal, I/O handling, texture mapping, lighting, alpha blending, special effects such as fogging and particles.

CTIS 491.name: Software Validation Verification and Testing
CTIS 491.description: Software inspections and reviews, requirements tracing, and system and component testing. Test planning, test case design, defect reporting and tracking, and control of testing process on sample software projects.

CTIS 492.name: Information Systems Outsourcing
CTIS 492.description: Fundamental concepts of information systems. Management information in organizations, decision support systems, enterprise resource planning, information systems is planning, organizing for information system projects, IS project lifecycle models, IS development and maintenance principles, organization, management and control IS, information technology (IT) and IT-enabled services outsourcing, voluntary and involuntary outsourcing for both consumers and producers of IT and IT-enabled service, variables that impact outsourcing and the impacts of outsourcing from business as well as social perspectives.

CTIS 493.name: Information Systems Project Management
CTIS 493.description: The project management discipline and the project management life cycle. The management of project teams and project communications, project selection, scheduling, and control tools and techniques such as Net Present Value (NPV), Return on Investment (ROI), Work Breakdown Structures (WBS), Critical Path Method (CPM), and Earned Value (EV) management Project risk, quality, and procurement management.

CTIS 496.name: Computer and Network Security
CTIS 496.description: Theory and practice of computer security, focusing in particular on the security aspects of computing systems. Survey of classical cryptography and cryptographic tools used to provide security, such as shared key encryption, cryptographic hash functions, public key encryption, key exchange, and digital signature. Review of how these tools are utilized in Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Transport-Level Security, Wireless Network Security, Electronic Mail Security. Introduction to "Network Access Control", "System Security", and "Secure Programming".

CTIS 497.name: Scaling Networks
CTIS 497.description: CCNA Routing and Switching -3: Introduction to scaling networks, LAN redundancy, link aggregation, wireless LANs, operation and configuring OSPF for IPv4 and IPv6, operation and configuring EIGRP for IPv4 and IPv6, troubleshooting networks.

CTIS 498.name: Wide Area Networks
CTIS 498.description: CCNA Exploration-4 : Introduction to Wide Area Networks: Circuit-switching vs Packet-switching. HDLC, PPP, Frame Relay protocol concepts and configuration. Introduction to Network Security. Using Access Control Lists to secure networks. Standard and extended ACL configuration. Teleworker Services: Broadband services: Cable, DSL and Wireless. Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). IP Addressing Services : DHCP, NAT, IPv6. Network troubleshooting.
